questions.passage: You save a few hours of free time, which presumably translates into more happiness. Ashley Whillans and colleagues found that, across 4,469 respondents, those who spent some money every month to save free time were happier than those who didn’t. This was in part explained by time stress measured by prompts such as, “I feel pressed for time today.” That is, those who spent money on time-saving services were less stressed about time, and the less stressed about time someone is, the more satisfied they are with their lives overall.
questions.prompt: What does the reported survey pattern support?
options: Time-saving spending was linked with greater happiness and lower time stress in the respondents.
All respondents became happier after being randomly given cleaning services.
Material purchases were experimentally shown to cause time stress in all 4,469 respondents.
Time stress completely explained every difference in life satisfaction.
questions.promptZh: 这里报告的调查模式支持什么？
optionsZh: 在受访者中，节省时间的支出与更幸福、较少时间压力相关。
所有受访者都被随机赠送清洁服务后变得更幸福。
实验表明实物购买使全部 4,469 人产生时间压力。
时间压力完全解释生活满意度的每一项差异。
analyses: A were happier 与 less stressed 描述样本中的联系，适合用 linked with 表述。
B respondents 不代表随机赠送服务；也没有 all 均改善的结果。
C 当前是调查，未给实物购买的实验比较。
D in part 明确只是部分解释，不能写成完全解释。presumably 与 survey 不能合并成已证明普遍因果。

evidence.quote: across 4,469 respondents, those who spent some money every month to save free time were happier than those who didn’t.
This was in part explained by time stress

questions.translation: 你省下几小时空闲时间，这想来会转化为更多幸福。Ashley Whillans 及同事发现，在 4,469 名受访者中，每月花一些钱来腾出空闲时间的人，比不这样做的人更幸福。这部分可以用时间压力解释；时间压力由“我今天觉得时间紧迫”这样的提示语测量。也就是说，花钱购买省时服务的人时间压力较小，而一个人越少为时间发愁，对整体生活就越满意。

questions.passage: Whillans and colleagues then conducted an experiment to test the causal role of time-saving spending. They gave participants $80 and told them to spend $40 on a time-saving service one weekend and spend the other $40 on a material purchase another weekend. Participants were contacted on the days they spent $40. Participants reported more positive emotions and less negative emotions after the time-saving spending than after the material purchase.
questions.prompt: When were participants contacted in the spending experiment?

Only three months before either purchase.

questions.translation: 随后，Whillans 及同事进行了实验，以检验省时支出的因果作用。他们给参与者八十美元，要求一个周末花四十美元购买省时服务，另一个周末把其余四十美元用于实物购买。研究者在参与者花这四十美元的当天联系他们。与买实物后相比，参与者报告在购买省时服务后有更多积极情绪、更少消极情绪。

evidence.quote: Whillans and colleagues then conducted an experiment to test the causal role of time-saving spending. They gave participants $80 and told them to spend $40 on a time-saving service one weekend and spend the other $40 on a material purchase another weekend. Participants were contacted on the days they spent $40. Participants reported more positive emotions and less negative emotions after the time-saving spending than after the material purchase.
